metadata.title: Zero Work Carrying a Box
metadata.register: formal, undergrad/grad audience, no casual narration
metadata.branding: none — unbranded, book content only, no channel/logo/handle

beats.narration_text: You carry a heavy box across a room at a steady pace. How much work do you do on the box?
beats.new_visual_element: Portrait-only opening question card (title-styled, crimson underline).

beats.narration_text: Carry a heavy box across a room at a steady pace. Your arms burn, and it certainly feels like hard work. Yet physics says that the work you do on the box is exactly zero.
beats.new_visual_element: A line-drawn stick figure carries a cardboard box, walking left to right along a dashed floor line; its arms tremble and small sweat drops appear above its head.
beats.accumulated_scene_state: stick figure walking with box on a dashed floor, sweat drops

beats.narration_text: Two vectors matter here. To hold the box up against gravity, you push upward on it; that is your force. Meanwhile, the box moves horizontally across the room; that is its displacement. The two are perpendicular.
beats.new_visual_element: The figure freezes mid-stride. A teal arrow F points straight up from the box's top corner; a vermilion arrow d points straight right from the same corner; a right-angle mark labeled 90° sits between them.
beats.accumulated_scene_state: frozen figure with box, upward force F, horizontal displacement d, 90° mark

beats.narration_text: Work is not force alone, and it is not motion alone. It is the force multiplied by the displacement and by the cosine of the angle between them: W equals F d cosine theta. Here the angle is ninety degrees, and the cosine of ninety degrees is zero.
beats.new_visual_element: Split screen: the frozen box-and-arrows drawing on one side; on the other, W = F d cos θ is written. θ is circled and linked by a dashed line to the 90° mark, then θ = 90° and cos 90° = 0 are written.
beats.accumulated_scene_state: split: static drawing | W = F d cos θ, θ = 90°, cos 90° = 0

beats.narration_text: So the work you do on the box is zero. Your muscles still consume energy, because their fibers must keep contracting to hold the load up. But that energy is spent inside your body. None of it is transferred to the box, which neither speeds up nor slows down.
beats.new_visual_element: W = 0 is written and double-underlined; the split closes. W = 0 becomes a stamp beside the box; the figure's arms glow vermilion and a thought bubble reads: muscle effort ≠ work on the box.
beats.accumulated_scene_state: full-screen figure with box, W = 0 stamp, glowing arms, thought bubble

beats.narration_text: A force acts, and the object moves, yet no work is done, because the force has no component along the displacement. Only the part of a force that lies along the motion can do work.
beats.new_visual_element: Stamp and bubble clear; the same F arrow, d arrow and 90° mark from before return; W = F d cos 90° = 0 is written across the bottom and a gold circle highlights the box.
beats.accumulated_scene_state: final held frame: figure, box, F, d, 90° mark, W = F d cos 90° = 0, box circled
